title: The Rough Patch
novel:
Barney and Robin had been together for months, and the [[spark|spark]] was gone. They bickered over small things. They stopped laughing. They had hit a [[rough patch|rough patch]].

Ted and Marshall [[hatched|hatch]] a plan. They would play [[matchmaker|matchmaker]] and set each of them up with someone new, hoping the [[jealousy|jealousy]] would [[force|force]] a confession.

But the plan [[backfired|backfire]]. Barney went on a date and liked it. Robin did the same. Neither seemed [[miserable|miserable]] enough to stop.

Finally Ted sat them down. "You're making each other [[unhappy|unhappy]]," he said. "Maybe you should [[break up|break up]]."

The words hung in the air. Barney and Robin looked at each other, and for a moment the old [[tenderness|tenderness]] flickered. Then they both [[nodded|nod]].

"We're better as friends," Robin said quietly.

They [[agreed|agree]] to end it before they grew to hate each other. Some loves, Ted realized, were not meant to last — but they were [[meant|mean]] to teach you something before they let you go.

spark.en: a feeling of excitement between two people

rough patch.en: a difficult period in a relationship

hatch.en: to make a plan, often in secret

matchmaker.en: a person who tries to bring two people together

jealousy.en: the angry feeling when someone you like is with another

backfire.en: to have the opposite result to what you wanted

nod.en: to move your head up and down to say yes

agree.en: to have the same opinion as someone

mean.en: to intend or be destined to do something
